## Problem

A handled signal without SA_RESTART interrupts the child-tree sentinel read in ExternalReplayer::wait(). The implementation logs the error, polls waitpid for about 100 ms, synthesizes success 0, and resets its PID while the child is still running.

## Evidence level

Reproduced against the unmodified ExternalReplayer implementation; independently rebuilt and rerun.

## Reproduction / verification status

Run the shared runner and inspect `external wait-interrupt`. A controlled helper stays alive; SIGALRM interrupts wait. Observed `wait_status=0 child_alive=1 handle=-1`. The harness individually kills/reaps its child afterwards.

[Probe source](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/c039c2b6c9997e78a6a4dd46df5ff1534eda7a62/local-docs/reviews/worker-lifecycle-audit-evidence/external_probe.cpp)

## Running the retained Linux evidence

On Linux with GCC, Python 3 and populated project submodules, check out evidence commit `c039c2b6c9997e78a6a4dd46df5ff1534eda7a62` from this fork and run:

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
python3 local-docs/reviews/worker-lifecycle-audit-evidence/reproduce.py --out /tmp/fresh-fossilize-lifecycle-evidence
```

The output directory must not already exist. Inspect the named case in `results.json`; generated binaries also accept the case arguments shown there. No Steam or real GPU workload is started. The runner matches observed defects, so a successful research-run exit does not certify corrected behavior.

## Required outcome and acceptance

- Retry EINTR or return a truthful interruption outcome without forgetting the live child; never synthesize successful completion from a live waitpid result.
- Use a deterministic signal/barrier test and assert process liveness, retained ownership, eventual cancellation/reaping and final status.
- Cover already-dead children, normal EOF, repeated wait after completion and fatal/nonretryable errors. Preserve the documented wait contract or explicitly document/test an intentional change.

## Scope and references

Fix/investigate the lifecycle boundary described above, including its regression coverage. Do not expand this into Steam scheduling policy, automatic deployment, a general scheduler rewrite or unrelated Vulkan behavior.

## Shared acceptance and evidence

This is a child of the worker lifecycle epic through GitHub's native hierarchy. Its shared verification/compatibility gates apply. Add deterministic assertion-bearing regression coverage that fails before the fix where feasible; retain healthy controls. These research probes expose defects and are not passing product tests.

Audit source: `556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec`; local audit baseline `2325a40846cceb9e053cc5b26aad4c030e07e1a2`. The relevant platform supervisor/owner headers remain unchanged in fork master `5eb2c496dde819c868fa3d7d1e52c51047d9adb8`. No claim is made about Steam's installed version, report frequency, or hardware cache behavior.

assertions: A real controlled child remains alive behind a pipe barrier, with a retained child-tree sentinel writer. Install a handled signal without SA_RESTART in the waiting owner.

Use a test-only read adapter and signal/barrier acknowledgements to establish that the real sentinel read returned -1/EINTR while the child was nonterminal; require actual handler execution and actual EINTR observation. Merely injecting errno or hoping a timer fires is insufficient for this case.

After interruption, wait has not reported successful completion, the owner still exposes the exact PID, and its cancellation/control descriptors remain usable. Observe owner state within the owner thread at the adapter/retry boundary, not via unsynchronized cross-thread API calls.

Release/cancel only after this observation: invoke the public kill() at a serialized test boundary using inherit_process_group=false, let wait collect -SIGKILL, require child reaped (waitpid yields ECHILD), invalidated handle and stable repeated cached status.
All helpers and process groups are accounted for and cleaned up even on failure. A finite watchdog bounds missing-event/deadlock failures; sleeps are not correctness barriers.

poll_progress invoked at wait entry can independently misclassify waitpid EINTR; fixing only sentinel read is insufficient. Keep changes narrow to status/ownership classification.
Test wrappers must target only the selected owner syscall/PID/phase, call real syscalls for liveness/reaping and stay out of shipped production library symbols/options.

## Problem

A handled signal without SA_RESTART interrupts the child-tree sentinel read in ExternalReplayer::wait(). The implementation logs the error, polls waitpid for about 100 ms, synthesizes success 0, and resets its PID while the child is still running.

## Evidence level

Reproduced against the unmodified ExternalReplayer implementation; independently rebuilt and rerun.

## Reproduction / verification status

Run the shared runner and inspect `external wait-interrupt`. A controlled helper stays alive; SIGALRM interrupts wait. Observed `wait_status=0 child_alive=1 handle=-1`. The harness individually kills/reaps its child afterwards.

[Probe source](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/c039c2b6c9997e78a6a4dd46df5ff1534eda7a62/local-docs/reviews/worker-lifecycle-audit-evidence/external_probe.cpp)

## Running the retained Linux evidence

On Linux with GCC, Python 3 and populated project submodules, check out evidence commit `c039c2b6c9997e78a6a4dd46df5ff1534eda7a62` from this fork and run:

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
python3 local-docs/reviews/worker-lifecycle-audit-evidence/reproduce.py --out /tmp/fresh-fossilize-lifecycle-evidence
```

The output directory must not already exist. Inspect the named case in `results.json`; generated binaries also accept the case arguments shown there. No Steam or real GPU workload is started. The runner matches observed defects, so a successful research-run exit does not certify corrected behavior.

## Required outcome and acceptance

- Retry EINTR or return a truthful interruption outcome without forgetting the live child; never synthesize successful completion from a live waitpid result.
- Use a deterministic signal/barrier test and assert process liveness, retained ownership, eventual cancellation/reaping and final status.
- Cover already-dead children, normal EOF, repeated wait after completion and fatal/nonretryable errors. Preserve the documented wait contract or explicitly document/test an intentional change.

## Scope and references

Fix/investigate the lifecycle boundary described above, including its regression coverage. Do not expand this into Steam scheduling policy, automatic deployment, a general scheduler rewrite or unrelated Vulkan behavior.

This is a child of the worker lifecycle epic through GitHub's native hierarchy. Its shared verification/compatibility gates apply. Add deterministic assertion-bearing regression coverage that fails before the fix where feasible; retain healthy controls. These research probes expose defects and are not passing product tests.
